# Udayajātaka (Ja 458)

**ID:** Ja 458
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Udayajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul10.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Ruling the prosperous city of Surundha, the couple maintain a life of absolute celibacy (*brahmacariya*) in a shared chamber for seven hundred years without succumbing to lust [Fausböll 1887; Silk 2009]. After dying first, the Bodhisatta is reborn as Sakka; he subsequently tests the queen's virtue, teaches her the Dhamma, and inspires her to renounce the world as an ascetic, where upon death she is reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven [Fausböll 1887]. At the conclusion of the sermon, the backsliding monk attains stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1887].

 DharmaNexus independently confirms Pali-internal reuse with SN 1 and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, while computing cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (scoring up to 95) and parallel segments in Chinese and Tibetan collections [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, the narrative was adapted into Sanskrit kavya in the *Haribhaṭṭajātakamālā* (*Udayajātaka*) [Martin 2006], and early visual depictions of the story are preserved among the Hinayana wall paintings of Cave 9 at Ajanta [Spink 2006].
